tokyo_maruju_yakiniku_ichigaya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the house specialty is tare-marinated kalbi and loin, and the meal ends with cold noodles and soups.
tokyo_maruju_yakiniku_ichigaya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a beef yakiniku with beef soups.
tokyo_maruju_yakiniku_ichigaya.hours_raw: Tabelog gives no hours. Reviewers: reservations needed by 18:00 and the shop closes at 21:00 (October 2026). Booking route: regulars and introductions only — no walk-ins, no new reservations; a first visit is with a regular, who explains the house rules (2026 reviews). Ice cream for dessert on Saturdays (August 2026). Gomtang soup not served in summer (June 2022). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). 20 seats, all tables; smoking allowed (Tabelog; October 2026). About ¥6,000–10,000 a head with drinks (2026 reviews).
tokyo_maruju_yakiniku_ichigaya.notes: [Yakiniku · Ichigaya, a regulars-only Showa yakiniku] A basement yakiniku that has kept the same crowd for decades — one regular counts 56 visits — and takes no new customers: you go with a regular, who briefs you on the house rules for ordering and even where to rest your chopsticks. What earns the loyalty is meat cut and seasoned in house: liver, salted tongue and loin, flap meat and Showa-style tare kalbi from heifers with light, sweet fat, then cold noodles or a beef soup. It is run by a couple, with the proprietress handling the whole dining room alone, briskly; reviewers call the proprietress "quite a character" and the value remarkable, under ¥10,000 with plenty to drink. Smoking allowed; cash only; book by 18:00.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owners. "It seems that the restaurant is run by a couple… there are certain manners to observe when entering and placing your order" (April 2026). "It was truly impressive to see just one person managing the entire dining area" (August 2026, a regular of 56 visits). An October 2026 first-timer describes a strong-willed proprietress managing the floor alone, "quite a character". "While it's not as strict as it used to be, there are still certain etiquette rules, like how to place your chopsticks" (October 2026). Many guests from the television industry on a Friday (October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Tare kalbi; liver; salted tongue and loin; flap meat.

anecdotes.text: "This charming restaurant, filled with the appeal of a bygone era, offers delicious tare kalbi that harks back to the Showa period, setting it apart from modern yakiniku places." — June 2022, a monthly visitor.
"Since they don't accept new reservations, I highly recommend visiting this yakiniku restaurant if you get the opportunity!" — May 2026.
"I drank a lot of alcohol and spent less than JPY 10,000… I can't believe such a place exists in Tokyo these days." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 丸十、焼肉、六番町4-11 朝日六番町マンション B1F、JR市ケ谷駅から日テレ通りをまっすぐ、坂の上の信号を渡ったビルの地下、営業時間の記載なし、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、20席、喫煙可、焼酎・ワイン。口コミ(2022年〜2026年): 昭和の味のタレカルビ、レバー、塩タン、塩ロース、ハラミ、カルビ、冷麺、未経産牛の肉、常連とその紹介のみで新規の予約は受けない、注文や箸の置き方などの決まり、夫婦で営む店で女将がひとりで客席を回す、予約は18時まで、21時閉店、1人1万円以下。

cultural_comfort.note: Introductions only; go with a regular, who explains the ordering etiquette.

existence.note: Tabelog listing; reviews dated through October 2026.

tokyo_toka_yakitori_ichigaya.gf_detail: Ask. Skewers come salted or with condiments such as mustard and red yuzu pepper, but courses include dashi dishes, soy-pickled ginkgo, a chicken-soup ramen and green curry; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_toka_yakitori_ichigaya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a chicken restaurant whose cooking is built on bonito dashi (Tabelog).
tokyo_toka_yakitori_ichigaya.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and holidays 17:30–23:30 (last order 22:30, last seating 22:00); closed Sunday and some other days, posted monthly; may close early when the yakitori sells out — call ahead (Tabelog). Seat availability posted daily on Instagram @touka.ichigaya (Tabelog). Reservations taken; same-day cancellations and late arrivals by phone (Tabelog). At least two drinks per person; no service charge (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 15 seats: 9 at the counter and a semi-private box for 4–6, served through a small window; hire up to 20; non-smoking (Tabelog). Some groups brought their own wine (June and September 2026).
tokyo_toka_yakitori_ichigaya.notes: [Yakitori · Ichigaya, a couple's basement counter for Hinai chicken and sake] Down a Showa-looking stair under Tonkatsu Kawamura, a clean white-wood counter where Hinai jidori is grilled over charcoal — crisp skin, juicy meat, the salt judged just right — between small Japanese dishes from a chef trained in both kitchens. The 14-dish, eight-skewer course is ¥7,300, and regulars add à la carte skewers, a cacao-topped liver pâté and the green curry that one diner would come back for alone. Over twenty sakes, many from Tohoku, come with handwritten notes from the owner. Run by a friendly couple with a mostly local, often business crowd; book ahead, two drinks minimum, open to 23:30.

chef_bio.background: No source names the chef or owner. Tabelog (shop text): hand-skewered yakitori and Japanese cuisine based on bonito dashi, by "a chef with experience in both yakitori and Japanese cuisine". Reviewers: "It is run by a friendly couple" (September 2026); "I also became a fan of the couple and the staff" (September 2026); "The chef in a neat happi coat and the owner in traditional attire and an apron" (September 2026); "The Japanese sake was carefully selected by the owner, focusing on options from the Tohoku region" (September 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Hinai jidori yakitori; shio tsukune; green curry.

anecdotes.text: "The green curry was so good that it could easily be served at a curry restaurant for lunch! Haha. I will definitely come back just for this curry!!!" — April 2026.
"I appreciated the thoughtful gesture of being able to take home the second serving of Hinai chicken and edamame rice as an onigiri." — June 2026.
"The owner kindly explained (and wrote down) the various types of Japanese sake and other drinks." — January 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗の紹介): 灯火、焼き鳥・日本料理・鶏料理、六番町4-11 朝日六番町マンション B1F、市ケ谷駅から徒歩3分、麹町駅4分、月〜土・祝17:30〜23:30 (L.O.22:30、最終入店22:00)、日曜と不定休、焼き鳥が売り切れたら早仕舞い、空席はインスタグラム @touka.ichigaya で毎日更新、1人2杯以上のドリンク注文、サービス料なし、カード可、15席 (カウンター9席と半個室のボックス席)、禁煙、手打ちの串とかつお出汁の日本料理、Hinai jidori の塩つくねと炊き込みご飯。口コミ(2025年〜2026年): 夫婦で営む、8本のおまかせコース (14品) 7,300円、レバーのパテ、グリーンカレー、親子丼、鶏のスープのラーメン、東北の日本酒が20種以上、手書きの説明。

cultural_comfort.note: Course or à la carte at the counter; the owner explains the sakes.

existence.note: Tabelog listing with October 2026 closing days; reviews dated through September 2026.

tokyo_tonkatsu_kawamura_ichigaya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: breaded, fried pork cutlets; katsu curry.
tokyo_tonkatsu_kawamura_ichigaya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork cutlets and pork miso soup.
tokyo_tonkatsu_kawamura_ichigaya.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and the days before and after holidays: lunch 11:00–14:30 (last order 14:00), dinner 17:30–21:00 (last order 20:30); Sundays and holidays lunch only (Tabelog). Dinner ends when ingredients sell out; lunch katsu sold out by 13:00 on an August 2026 Sunday (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Reservations taken; held 15 minutes (Tabelog); waiting customers outside at an October 2026 lunch. Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). 19 seats: 11 at the counter and two tables of 4; non-smoking; English menu; school-age children welcome (Tabelog). Opened 27 May 2020 (Tabelog).
tokyo_tonkatsu_kawamura_ichigaya.notes: [Tonkatsu · Ichigaya, a calm modern counter for Hayashi SPF pork] A modern Japanese tonkatsu room on Nittere-dōri, the original of a two-shop company that also runs a branch at Azabudai Hills. The pork is Hayashi SPF, fried with a light, crisp crust: loin with sweet fat, tender fillet, or both, eaten with salt, sauce or wasabi soy sauce; reviewers single out the rice and a hearty pork miso soup. Lunch sets run about ¥1,800–2,000; the limited katsu sells out early. Small gripes: cabbage refills limited to one, dressing only on request, room-temperature pickles. Book for lunch — lines form; dinner ends when the pork runs out.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 27 May 2020 by SHIN Dining Co., Ltd.; a second shop at Azabudai Hills (company website).
chef_bio.background: Company website: SHIN Dining Co., Ltd. (株式会社SHIN Dining, representative director 岩松 智洋) runs "Tonkatsu Kawamura" in Ichigaya and at Azabudai Hills; founded in 2020, now in its sixth year; the Ichigaya shop serves the everyday business crowd, the Azabudai Hills shop international guests. No source names the chef. Tabelog (shop text): "Hayashi SPF" pork, with attention to cooking method, salt, oil and sauce.
chef_bio.philosophy: To serve a dish that lets you feel 『沁』 (SHIN) — not to attract with flashiness but with a quiet space (company website, translated).
chef_bio.specialty: Loin and fillet katsu of Hayashi SPF pork.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the 'Lunch Premium Loin' (JPY 1950). The rich pork soup and the lightly pickled cabbage on the table added a unique touch to the meal… This is the best tonkatsu I've had recently." — September 2026.
"I enjoyed it with salt, sauce, and wasabi soy sauce, and I found that the wasabi soy sauce brought out the meat's flavor the best." — October 2026, mixed cutlet set.
"I only got one refill of cabbage. I later found out that the dressing is served upon request, which was a downside for me." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 会社の公式サイト: 株式会社SHIN Dining (代表取締役 岩松 智洋) が市ヶ谷と麻布台ヒルズの2店舗で「とんかつ河むら」を営む、2020年創業、6期目、市ヶ谷店はビジネスパーソンの日常に寄り添う料理。食べログ: とんかつ、六番町4-11 朝日六番町マンション 1F、市ケ谷駅3番出口から徒歩4分、麹町駅6番出口から3分、月〜土・祝前日・祝後日 11:00〜14:30 (L.O.14:00)・17:30〜21:00 (L.O.20:30)、日祝はランチのみ、夜は売り切れ次第終了、予約は15分過ぎで取り消し、カード・電子マネー・QR可、19席 (カウンター11席と4人掛け2卓)、禁煙、英語メニューあり、2020年5月27日オープン、「Hayashi SPF」の豚。口コミ(2026年): ランチの上ロース1,950円、ヒレかつカレー1,800円、豚汁、キャベツのおかわりは1回、漬物は食べ放題、塩・ソース・わさび醤油。

existence.note: Tabelog listing and company website (2026); reviews dated through October 2026.

tokyo_fruit_cafe_pomp_ningyocho.gf_detail: Ask. Kakigori is shaved ice with fruit and syrups, but parfaits include granola (2026 reviews); nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_fruit_cafe_pomp_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: milk syrups, whipped cream and ice cream on most items; ask about fruit-only syrups.
tokyo_fruit_cafe_pomp_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Fri and the days before and after holidays 13:30–19:30 (last order 19:00); Sat, Sun and holidays 13:00–18:30 (last order 18:00); changes and typhoon closures posted on Instagram and X (Tabelog). Reservations by email or Instagram DM; please be on time (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Cards, transport IC, Edy, nanaco, WAON, iD, QUICPay, PayPay and other QR (Tabelog). 14 counter seats (Tabelog). Opened 29 July 2019 (Tabelog). Featured on the TV show ZIP! (Tabelog).
tokyo_fruit_cafe_pomp_ningyocho.notes: [Sweets · Ningyocho, peach kakigori and whole-peach parfaits] A fourteen-seat counter café devoted to fruit, best known for its Okayama white-peach season: fluffy kakigori under heaps of sliced peach with milk syrup (¥2,200 small), and parfaits crowned with a whole Shimizu Hakuto peach over ice cream, granola and acai (about ¥4,900 with a drink for two peaches). Out of peach season there are other fruits, such as Shine Muscat with homemade syrup. Diners call it a splurge — prices are high — but the fruit quality is the point. Book by Instagram DM or email, especially in peach season; weekday afternoons can be walk-in. It has appeared on ZIP!. Opens from 13:00 or 13:30.

chef_bio.background: Opened 29 July 2019 (Tabelog). The Okayama white-peach menu is the shop's most popular (Tabelog shop text). Featured on ZIP!, with acrylic stands from the visit on display (Tabelog; July 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Luxuriously piled with the finest fruits. Fruits are the main attraction." (Tabelog shop text)
chef_bio.specialty: Okayama white peach kakigori and parfaits.

anecdotes.text: "At the top, there’s a whole juicy peach, creating an impressive visual impact." — July 2026, peach parfait.
"The peaches were of the Okayama Shimizu Hakuto variety and were medium-sized." — August 2026.
"However, it is a bit pricey, so I can't come here too often." — July 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: フルーツカフェ pomp、カフェ、かき氷、日本橋人形町2-21-4 加藤ビル 1F、人形町駅A1出口から徒歩2分、月〜金・祝前日・祝後日13:30〜19:30、土日祝13:00〜18:30、営業の変更は Instagram と X で、予約はメールか Instagram の DM、カード・電子マネー・QR可、カウンター14席、2019年7月29日オープン、Okayama の白桃のメニューが人気、ZIP! で紹介。口コミ(2026年7月〜9月): 白桃ミルクのかき氷 (小) 2,200円、大は桃が丸ごと、アールグレイ白桃のかき氷1,980円、桃のチャイのかき氷、シャインマスカット、清水白桃を丸ごとのせたパフェ (バニラアイス、グラノーラ、アサイー)、桃2個のパフェとドリンクで約4,900円、値段は高め、平日の昼は予約なしでも入れることも。

cultural_comfort.note: Book by Instagram DM in peach season; counter only.

existence.note: Tabelog official listing; reviews dated July–September 2026.

tokyo_soyoichi_ningyocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: breaded beef and pork cutlets, menchi katsu and croquettes; the pork sauté is finished with soy sauce.
tokyo_soyoichi_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef and pork dishes, served with tonjiru (pork miso soup).
tokyo_soyoichi_ningyocho.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 11:00–14:00 and 17:30–20:00; closed Sunday, Monday and other irregular days (Tabelog). No reservations; queues by noon (2026 reviews). Cards, e-money, PayPay and au PAY; no service charge (Tabelog). 15 counter seats around the kitchen; non-smoking (Tabelog). Opened 7 October 2008 (Tabelog). Free rice refills (2026 reviews).
tokyo_soyoichi_ningyocho.notes: [Yoshoku · Ningyocho, the beef cutlet and pork sauté of old Kiraku] A fifteen-seat counter yoshoku in a back alley, opened in 2008 by the daughter of the owner of Yoshoku Kiraku (founded 1946) to carry on its dishes (October 2026). The owner runs a fast, flawless kitchen in front of you (September 2026). Everyone comes for two plates: a crisp, tender beef cutlet and a thick pork sauté flambéed in butter and soy sauce, with garlic if you like, each about ¥2,200 with pork miso soup and free rice refills. Ten servings a day of menchi katsu and, after 13:00, katsu curry. A Tabelog Yoshoku 100 pick in 2020 and 2022; queues form by noon. One diner wished for more sauce choices than chuno and Worcestershire (October 2026).

roles: Owner-chef, the daughter of the previous owner of Yoshoku Kiraku (October 2026 review); "the chef (the owner)" (September 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Opened 7 October 2008 (Tabelog), carrying on the flavours of Yoshoku Kiraku, founded in 1946 (September, October 2026 reviews); the Tabelog menu describes the pork sauté as carrying on the same flavour from the previous generation of Kiraku. Selected for Tabelog Yoshoku 100 in 2020 and 2022 (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I watched as the efficient chef (the owner) prepared the dishes with … usual flawless operation" — September 2026.
"Suddenly, there was a burst of flames, and it turned out to be the pork sauté being flambéed." — October 2026.
"The previous owner's daughter, who now runs the place, is renowned for … delicious Western cuisine" — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: そよいち、洋食、洋食百名店2020・2022、日本橋人形町1-9-6、人形町駅から徒歩2分、火〜土11:00〜14:00、17:30〜20:00、日・月休み、不定休、予約不可、カード・電子マネー・QR可、サービス料なし、カウンター15席、禁煙、2008年10月7日オープン、ビーフカツ2,200円、ポークカツ2,000円、ポークソテー2,200円 (先代の Kiraku の味を受け継ぐ)、ハンバーグ1,550円、ハヤシライス1,800円、豚汁とご飯のおかわり。口コミ(2026年9月〜10月): 1946年創業の洋食 Kiraku の味を継ぐ、先代の娘さんが営む、手際のよい厨房、フランベするポークソテー、ビーフカツ (2,400円という声も)、10食限定のメンチカツ定食1,400円、13時からのカツカレー1,450円、昼は行列、ソースの種類がもう少しほしいという声も。

cultural_comfort.note: Counter only; queue at lunch; say if you want garlic on the pork sauté.

tokyo_365_salongo_cafe_ningyocho.gf_detail: Ask. The lunch side dishes change daily (curries, stews, salads) and sandwiches are on the menu; nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_365_salongo_cafe_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: daily side dishes include chicken stew and minced meat; vegetable sides appear (2022 reviews) — ask.
tokyo_365_salongo_cafe_ningyocho.hours_raw: Lunch Mon–Fri 11:00–14:00; evenings Tue, Thu and Fri 18:00–24:00, Wed 18:30–24:00, Sat and Sun 18:00–24:00 (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; private hire up to 20 (Tabelog). No credit cards at lunch; cards in the evening (Tabelog). 17 seats (Tabelog). Non-smoking at lunch; smoking permitted during bar time (Tabelog). Mostly takeaway at lunch, with tables to eat in (2022–25 reviews). Live music events in the evening (July 2025).
tokyo_365_salongo_cafe_ningyocho.notes: [Café · Ningyocho, a rice-bowl lunch counter that turns into a music bar] A small café a few minutes from Ningyocho, where weekday lunch is "bukkake rice": pick two, three or all four of the day's side dishes, from coconut curries and a Malaysian chicken stew to salads, piled over rice for well under ¥1,000, mostly taken away by office workers (2022–25 reviews). In the evening it becomes a bar with live music, open until midnight, where one 2025 visitor came for a friend's gig and stayed for the moussaka. The master is kind and welcoming (2017). One 2022 diner found some sides under-seasoned. Lunch is cash only; smoking is allowed at night. Recent reviews are few, so check before going.

roles: The master (unnamed; "a kind heart", December 2017 review)
chef_bio.background: A café with lunch bento and a music bar at night, hosting live performances (Tabelog; July 2025). The Tabelog lunch menu dates from 2020; reviews run from 2017 to 2025.
chef_bio.specialty: Bukkake rice with daily side dishes.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the '4 Dishes (All Included)' (JPY 800)." — April 2022: green curry, Malaysian-style chicken stew, spring cabbage with salt kombu, tofu-okra-wakame salad.
"I visited for a friend's live performance for the first time." — July 2025.
"The stir-fried minced meat was a classic version, and while the flavor was decent, it could have been better seasoned." — July 2022.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 365 サロンゴカフェ、カフェ、カレー、創作料理、日本橋人形町1-8-2 谷津ビル 1F、人形町駅・水天宮前駅から徒歩3分、昼は月〜金11:00〜14:00、夜は火曜・木曜・金曜18:00〜24:00、水曜18:30〜24:00、土日18:00〜24:00、予約可、貸切20名まで、昼はカード不可、17席、昼は禁煙・バーの時間は喫煙可、ホームページ cafe-salongo.com、昼のぶっかけご飯 (日替わりのおかず2品700円・3品750円・4品800円、2020年のメニュー)。口コミ(2017年9月〜2025年10月): 持ち帰りが多い、グリーンカレー、マレーシア風チキンシチュー、イエローカレー、4品の弁当900円 (2025年6月)、夜はライブ、ムサカ、味付けが物足りないおかずもという声。

cultural_comfort.note: Point at the day's side dishes; lunch cash only.

existence.note: Tabelog official listing; the latest reviews are from June–October 2025.

tokyo_fukuda_masayuki_soba_ningyocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the ni-hachi and arabiki soba contain wheat, the dipping sauce is soy-based, and there is tempura. 100% buckwheat (ju-wari) soba is offered, but the sauce still has soy (2025–26 reviews).
tokyo_fukuda_masayuki_soba_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: soba sauce made with bonito dashi; duck, pork and fish toppings.
tokyo_fukuda_masayuki_soba_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon 11:00–15:00; Tue–Fri breakfast 07:00–08:45 and lunch 11:00–15:00; Sun and holidays 11:00–14:30, not every week; closed Saturday (Tabelog). Evenings by reservation only (October 2026). Opening days posted on the website and LINE (Tabelog). No reservations for lunch; orders are taken while you wait and tables are shared (October 2026). QR codes accepted (PayPay, d Barai, au PAY); no cards or e-money (Tabelog). 6 seats: a table for four and one for two (October 2026). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Arabiki soba can sell out by a late lunch (December 2025).
tokyo_fukuda_masayuki_soba_ningyocho.notes: [Soba · Ningyocho, coarse-ground hand-made soba, breakfast from 7 a.m.] A six-seat soba shop in a back alley, named for its owner Masayuki Fukuda, who worked at a milling company in Tochigi before making soba (April 2025). The draw is arabiki soba: thick, rustic, coarse-ground noodles with a deep buckwheat flavour, a generous 300 g for ¥1,000. Ju-wari (all-buckwheat) and ni-hachi are also offered, with tempura, duck or tororo. On weekdays it opens at 7:00 for breakfast sets of soba with rice, salad and an onsen egg. Seating is shared and orders are taken in the queue, so the wait is short. No cards or e-money, but QR payment works. Closed Saturdays; evenings by reservation.

roles: Owner ("The owner, who has experience working at a milling company in Tochigi Prefecture, is a skilled chef", April 2025 review); the shop bears the name Fukuda Masayuki
chef_bio.background: Per reviews: the owner worked at a milling company in Tochigi Prefecture (April 2025); the shop is named after the owner (October 2026). Evenings are by reservation only (October 2026).

anecdotes.text: "It comes in a generous 300g portion for just JPY 1000, which is a great value!" — October 2026, arabiki soba.
"I arrived at 7:10, and out of the six seats, three were already taken." — October 2026, breakfast soba.
"Since I arrived for a late lunch, the Arabiki Soba was sold out, and only the Ju-wari Soba was available." — December 2025.

tokyo_up_to_you_coffee_matsugaya.gf_detail: GF — ask: coffee itself has no gluten, but the banana bread, toast and sandwiches are wheat-based; nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_up_to_you_coffee_matsugaya.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: black coffee is vegan, but no plant milk is mentioned and the cakes are not described.
tokyo_up_to_you_coffee_matsugaya.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–18:00 (Tabelog; may change). No reservations. Cash only (August 2026; Tabelog lists no cards, e-money or QR). 8 seats: a table for two and benches with small tables. Take-away +¥30. Non-smoking.
tokyo_up_to_you_coffee_matsugaya.notes: [Coffee · Kappabashi, Australian-style coffee in a tiny room] A tiny specialty coffee bar a short walk from Kappabashi kitchen-tool street, run by an owner known in latte art who, like the staff, trained in Australia, and who says the shop placed third in a world competition in the US. Expect flat whites, lattes with your choice of beans, a ristretto 'Magic' and bright light-roast pour-overs, with banana bread or a salad sandwich. Eight seats on benches; cash only. Most reviewers loved the coffee; one July 2026 diner found the iced drip too strong and half-warm, and a September 2026 diner noticed the cake was reheated from frozen.

chef_bio.background: Per a June 2026 review, run by an owner well known in the latte-art world; a July 2026 review says the owner and staff trained in Australia and the shop placed third in a world competition in the US. No source names the owner.

anecdotes.text: "I decided to try the Magic, which is made with a double shot of ristretto (a concentrated espresso)." — July 2026, ¥700.
"When the coffee arrived, I was immediately struck by its rich aroma." — June 2026, light roast.
"I felt a bit sad to see that the cake wasn't freshly baked but rather heated from frozen." — September 2026, banana cake.

tokyo_chacha_tei_uguisudani.vegan_detail: Not vegan: banmen is topped with shredded meat, chashu and a seasoned egg; ramen with back fat.
tokyo_chacha_tei_uguisudani.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–1:30 (Tabelog; may change). No reservations. Cash only. Non-smoking. Opened about September 2025 (a 1st-anniversary offer in September 2026).
tokyo_chacha_tei_uguisudani.notes: [Mixed noodles · Uguisudani, banmen until 1:30 am] A small noodle shop near Uguisudani Station serving banmen, a Chinese-style mixed noodle: thick, chewy noodles that you toss with a salt or soy tare from the bottom of the bowl, with a soft egg, green onion, menma, shredded meat and a squeeze of lemon (¥750). Add the spicy miso from the table if you want heat. There is ramen too, including a back-fat bowl, and the shop opens from 11:00 until 1:30, making it a late-night stop after drinks around Uguisudani. Cash only. The exterior can look off-putting, but reviewers in 2026 found the food light and satisfying.

chef_bio.origin: Opened about September 2025 (1st-anniversary offer, September 2026 review)

"While it's not very spicy on its own, you can add the spicy miso on the table to kick up the heat significantly." — August 2026.
"However, the taste is surprisingly refreshing and not overly strong." — September 2026, banmen.

tokyo_tako_kyuu_ueno.gf_detail: GF — ask: oden in a light soy-sauce broth, with fish cakes such as hanpen; sashimi and grilled fish are on the menu too, but nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_tako_kyuu_ueno.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the oden broth and fish cakes are fish-based; sashimi, saikyo-grilled fish, octopus, oysters.
tokyo_tako_kyuu_ueno.hours_raw: Wed–Sun 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); closed Mondays and Tuesdays (Tabelog). Reservations needed — by phone Wed–Sun from 12:00, or by Instagram DM; in the winter season (October–March) bookings are for 18:00–19:00 or after 20:15, seats are limited to 1.5 hours (2 hours otherwise), and walk-ins are taken if there is room. Appetizer ¥330. Cash only. 20 seats (14 at the counter, 6 at tables). Non-smoking (smoking outside). Take-out.
tokyo_tako_kyuu_ueno.notes: [Oden · Yushima, a traditional oden counter by the station] A long-established oden izakaya a minute from Yushima Station, behind a white noren, where the owner ladles oden from a big copper pot behind the counter: soft, sweet daikon, eggs, hanpen, whelk, potatoes and kinchaku in a light soy broth. Around it are good sashimi, saikyo-grilled fish and simple pickles, with sake and shōchū. It feels nostalgic and calm, and suits solo diners too (October 2026). Booking is the rule, especially from October to March, when slots are 18:00–19:00 or after 20:15 and tables turn after 90 minutes; cash only, closed Mondays and Tuesdays. One April 2026 diner called the staff quirky.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog official listing; a June 2026 review describes the owner serving oden from a large pot behind the counter. No source names the owner.

anecdotes.text: "Inside, the entrance features a large copper pot filled with oden, making a powerful impression." — October 2026.
"The flavors were incredibly comforting, with a gentle broth that wasn't too strong, making it perfect to pair with drinks." — October 2026.
"Quirky staff, but the seasonal dishes and potato oden are truly delightful." — April 2026.

tokyo_yakitori_oden_sakaji_ichigaya.gf_detail: Ask. Skewers come with tare or salt, the oden broth is salt-based, and there are fried dishes such as chicken nanban and fried yuba; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_yakitori_oden_sakaji_ichigaya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: oden in dashi broth, chicken skewers; Tabelog lists vegetarian options, but the broths are dashi.
tokyo_yakitori_oden_sakaji_ichigaya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri lunch 11:30–14:30 and dinner 17:00–23:30; Sat, Sun and holidays 17:00–23:30; irregular closing days (Tabelog). Reservations taken, online 24 hours; walk-ins at the counter (Tabelog; December 2025). ¥550 cover charge, included in courses (Tabelog; February 2026). Cards and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 60 seats: 6 at the counter, private booths and a kotatsu room; partitions do not reach the ceiling (May 2026); private hire 20–50; smoking allowed (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Opened 30 November 2021 (Tabelog).
tokyo_yakitori_oden_sakaji_ichigaya.notes: [Izakaya · Ichigaya, yakitori and salt-broth oden in private booths] A wood-and-stone izakaya on the fourth floor of the GEMS Ichigaya restaurant building, where almost every seat is a booth. Oden comes in a clear, gentle salt broth — daikon that falls apart, a soft egg, beef tendon — alongside yakitori with tare or salt and small dishes like chilled stuffed peppers and dashimaki, then oyakodon or a broth-poured chazuke to finish. Weekday lunch sets run ¥1,000–1,300. Not everyone was won over: the booths' partitions stop short of the ceiling, one diner found the staff low on energy, and a lunch chicken nanban seemed small for ¥1,200. Smoking allowed; ¥550 cover; open to 23:30.

chef_bio.background: No source names the chef or owner. Tabelog (shop text): yakitori of premium local chicken, year-round oden, seasonal obanzai and carefully chosen regional sake, in a calm room of natural wood and stone with private seating throughout. A January 2026 diner noted "the chef's attention to detail" in a whelk appetizer.

anecdotes.text: "The oden served first had a beautifully clear broth, and its refined flavor spread gently with each bite. The Japanese radish was so tender it fell apart with chopsticks." — February 2026, course.
"Although it was advertised as having all private rooms, the partitions didn't reach the ceiling, so conversations might leak over to the next table." — May 2026.
"It's a rare find these days as a 'smoking-friendly' establishment, making it very convenient for gatherings where some guests smoke." — April 2026.

tokyo_certo_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. Handmade pasta, gratins and risotto are on the menu; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_certo_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options; dishes seen in reviews lean on cheese, meat and seafood.
tokyo_certo_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–24:00 (last order 22:30); closed Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Mondays irregular since January 2026 — open if booked ahead (website). Dinner only since 2017 (Tabelog). Reservations taken; a second-floor private room in the house next door for one group a day (Tabelog; October 2026). ¥550 appetizer charge (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay or au PAY (Tabelog). 25 seats; non-smoking; English menu and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). Take-out, chilled dishes to cook at home and wine sales; Australian wine dinners, e.g. Margaret River on 27 October 2026, ¥15,000 (website). Opened in Yotsuya-sanchome on 15 December 2006 (Tabelog).
tokyo_certo_yotsuya.notes: [Italian · Yotsuya-sanchome, a Sydney-born trattoria with Australian wines] A small house restaurant down a back alley off Shinjuku-dōri that began in Sydney in 1999 as Italian cooking by a Japanese chef with Australian produce, and moved its name to Tokyo in 2006; one diner who knew it in Sydney found the same owner and waitress still here. The list is almost all Australian and New Zealand wine, and the waitress knows it well; the food is homely trattoria fare — liver pâté, tripe gratin, handmade tagliatelle, a lamb main that one diner called the best ever. Regulars count dozens of visits; a February 2026 guest found the courses slow and the room loud. Dinner only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.origin: Opened in Sydney in 1999; in Yotsuya-sanchome since 15 December 2006 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: No source names the chef or owner. Tabelog (shop text): "Certo was born in 1999 in Sydney, Australia. It started as a unique restaurant serving Italian cuisine crafted by a Japanese chef using fresh Australian ingredients. The restaurant has won numerous awards and has been featured in local newspapers." A diner who had visited in Sydney "was surprised to see the owner and waitress from back then still here" (October 2023); another found the chef "relatively young, but quite skilled" (June 2022).

anecdotes.text: "This was a nostalgic place I visited several times in Sydney♪ I was surprised to see the owner and waitress from back then still here." — October 2023.
"The lamb was the best I've ever had… the affogato was the best I've ever had!" — November 2024.
"The food came out one dish at a time every 30 minutes, and I wish I had just left without ordering a main dish." — February 2026.

tokyo_peasant_yonbancho_ichigaya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: breaded chicken katsu, fried oysters, katsu curry and hayashi sauce.
tokyo_peasant_yonbancho_ichigaya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: meat and fish set meals with miso soup and a raw egg.
tokyo_peasant_yonbancho_ichigaya.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 12:00–18:00; closed Sunday and holidays (Tabelog — "hours may change"). A June 2026 diner ate there at 18:00 on a weekday. No reservations; queues on the stairs and pavement around 13:00 (Tabelog; October 2026). Cash only (Tabelog; June 2026). 18 seats in the basement, counter and tables; non-smoking (Tabelog).
tokyo_peasant_yonbancho_ichigaya.notes: [Set meals · Ichigaya, a cheap and fast basement diner] Down a stair on Nittere-dōri under a weathered blue sign reading "Bancho Shokudo", an old, dim, cramped diner where ¥850 still buys the Yonbancho set: chicken katsu and ginger pork with a mound of rice, a big bowl of miso soup and a raw egg for tamago-kake-gohan. Hayashi rice, katsu curry, hamburg steak and fried oysters all come in under ¥1,000, and food lands within minutes of ordering. The owner passes plates over the counter with a word of warning when they are heavy; regulars and students queue on the stairs at one o'clock. One diner found the katsu hayashi sauce watery. Cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner. Reviewers: "the chef handed me a plate with everything except the main dish… kindly warned me, 'Be careful, it's heavy'" (October 2026); "The owner managed to squeeze me into a spot at the back of the counter… The charming interactions with the beloved owner and customers added to the experience" (October 2026). The sign reads "Bancho Shokudo", with "Peasant" in smaller letters (August 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Yonbancho set (chicken katsu and ginger pork).

anecdotes.text: "I raised four fingers and ordered the Yonbancho Set Meal for JPY 850… After settling the bill, I noticed four or five people waiting on the stairs and three or four more on the sidewalk." — October 2026.
"In deep ocean-like blue, the yellow letters boldly say 'Bancho Shokudo.' Next to it, the name 'Peasant' is written in smaller letters." — August 2026.
"The fried oysters were crispy and quite large, with four pieces served… At under JPY 1000, it offers excellent value for money." — October 2026.

Bread to take away from 11:30; weekends and holidays only 8 popular items (website); take-out customers walk straight in (October 2026). Orders by QR code; coffee refills free (October 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). 48 seats with a terrace; pets only on the engawa space; non-smoking; children and strollers welcome (Tabelog). Opened 1 December 2015 (Tabelog).
tokyo_no4_yonbancho_ichigaya.notes: [Café · Ichigaya, the bakery café with the queue] A bakery café with a leafy terrace in quiet Yonbanchō, open from 8 a.m. for French toast of yudane brioche with salted whipped butter, then wood-fired pizza and, at night, craft beer from the same company's T.Y.HARBOR brewery. The seasonal French toasts — pumpkin in October, sakura in April — draw regulars every year, and the bread counter (croissants, country loaves, quiche, sausage Danish) is worth the trip alone. The catch is the wait: two hours on a Sunday, 38th in line before ten, many overseas visitors among them; take-out buyers walk straight in. Prices run high and drinks are extra. Open daily.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 1 December 2015 by Tysons & Company (website; Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: No source names a chef. Website: "Not a café, not a restaurant, not a bakery. No.4 is a space to enjoy 'handcraft' freely from morning to night" (translated); run by Tysons & Company, which also brews T.Y.HARBOR beer. A reviewer bought bread from Breadworks Omotesando, "which seems to be part of the same chain" (October 2026) — a sister brand.
chef_bio.philosophy: "The most important element in food is people" (website recruiting page, translated).

anecdotes.text: "Every year, I look forward to the Pumpkin French Toast at No.4… this time it was JPY 2480, which is a JPY 100 increase." — October 2026, a seventh visit.
"We arrived at 11:05 and ended up waiting for over two hours. We finally got in around 13:40." — October 2026, a Sunday.
"If you opt for takeout, you can surprisingly get in quite easily. The display of delicious breads is impressive." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: No.4、カフェでもレストランでもベーカリーでもない、朝から晩まで「ハンドクラフト」を楽しめる空間、四番町5-9、予約は17:30以降、テイクアウトは11時30分から、土日祝は人気の8品のみ。食べログ: カフェ・パン・ピザ、麹町駅・市ケ谷駅から徒歩5分、毎日8:00〜21:00 (L.O.料理20:00、ドリンク20:30)、朝食8:00〜10:45、年末年始休み、カード・電子マネー・QR可、48席、テラス、禁煙、2015年12月1日オープン、国産小麦のパン、薪窯のピザ、T.Y.HARBOR のクラフトビール。口コミ(2025年〜2026年): フレンチトースト1,680〜1,740円、かぼちゃのフレンチトースト2,480円、コーヒーはおかわり自由、長い行列、テイクアウトはすぐ入れる。
